elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: New Article XII-A says only "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee"; there is no "defend" (or "hold harmless") obligation and no reference to Licensee's affiliates. The only defence duty in the document runs the other way (Article XII: "Licensee shall defend, indemnify, and hold Licensor harmless").

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A indemnifies "Licensee" only; affiliates of Licensee are not named as indemnified parties (contrast Article XII, which expressly protects "Licensor or any of its affiliates, directors, officers, employees, or agents").

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates such third party's intellectual property rights" — Licensed Technology is the defined licensed deliverable (Licensed Know-How plus Licensed Software).

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A is confined to third-party IP infringement/misappropriation claims; no limb covers Licensor's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No limb addressing unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee data caused by Licensor appears in Article XII-A or elsewhere.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no gross negligence or wilful misconduct limb, and Article XIII's retained damages exclusion still expressly covers claims "BASED UPON ... TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE)".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A contains no notice mechanic; nothing requires Licensee to notify Licensor of a claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: No provision allocates conduct/control of the defence or settlement; the only Licensor election is "at its option, procure ... modify or replace", which is a remedy choice, not defence control.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: No cooperation obligation appears in Article XII-A or any adjacent inserted text.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Article XII is left untouched and remains broad: Licensee indemnifies for "Licensee's exercise of any license or other rights", "the conduct of Licensee's business", and any breach of "any representation, warranty, obligation, restriction, term and/or covenant".

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Inserted Article XII-A: "Licensor shall indemnify Licensee against any third-party claim that the Licensed Technology infringes or misappropriates such third party's intellectual property rights." The conforming carve-out in Article XIII(a) ("EXCEPT FOR LICENSOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A") prevents the retained infringement disclaimer from negating it.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A carve-out (i): "modifications to the Licensed Technology made by Licensee".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Article XII-A carve-out (ii): "combination of the Licensed Technology with items not supplied by Licensor".

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: "Licensor shall, at its option, procure for Licensee the right to continue using, or modify or replace, the affected Licensed Technology."

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: "[I]f none of those remedies is reasonably available, Licensor shall refund the fees paid by Licensee for the affected Licensed Technology." The refund is expressly conditioned on unavailability of the other remedies.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: "Licensor's aggregate liability under this Article XII-A shall not exceed three (3) times the annual fees paid by Licensee to Licensor under this Agreement," and Article XIII(b) is conformed ("EXCEPT FOR LICENSOR'S INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS UNDER ARTICLE XII-A") so the one-half-of-amounts-paid general cap does not swallow the super-cap.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Duplicate-facing check: the same Article XII-A grant supports the preferred IP limb, but the preferred level still fails on defend, affiliates, non-IP limbs, procedure and the narrowed Licensee indemnity.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete: all seven elements (IP indemnity, three customary exclusions, procure/modify/replace, conditional refund, 3× annual-fees super-cap) appear in operative language in the inserted Article XII-A.

The two conforming edits to Article XIII are necessary, not cosmetic: without the carve-out from "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE ... INFRINGEMENT" the new indemnity would be internally contradicted, and without the carve-out from the one-half-of-amounts-paid aggregate cap the 3× super-cap element could not operate. No other retained words were deleted or paraphrased.
No extras were added — no survival tail, no attorneys'-fees or damages-category expansion, no notice/control/cooperation procedure beyond the fallback checklist — so minimality holds.

Intent is preserved: the existing Licensee indemnity in Article XII, the consequential-damages exclusion, and the general liability cap all survive unchanged apart from the two express carve-outs; the new Article XII-A cross-references are internally consistent and introduce no undefined terms (Licensed Technology, Licensor, Licensee are all defined).

Preferred level is not reached. To upgrade, the drafter must (a) change "shall indemnify" to "shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless", (b) extend the indemnified parties to "Licensee and its affiliates", (c) add limbs for Licensor's breach of applicable law, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Licensee data caused by Licensor, and Licensor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct, (d) add a notice / defence-control / reasonable-cooperation procedure, and (e) narrow Article XII so the Licensee indemnity is limited to Licensee-provided content and Licensee's breach of law (the current "conduct of Licensee's business" and all-covenant-breach limbs are far broader).

Claimed status "deviation" is correct on the original text: the pre-redline document had a one-way Licensee indemnity plus an express Licensor infringement disclaimer, which is at or beyond walk-away, and the redline targets the fallback.
